walk.title: Solve it: will it rain on tomorrow's deliveries?
walk.sample: Ibadan forecast from Open-Meteo · a fake payment.success webhook for order HL-0042

steps.say: Two jobs today, both by hand: ask a weather service about tomorrow's rain, then watch a payment notice arrive. No platform yet, so you see what the platforms hide.
Open-Meteo is free and needs no key for non-commercial use. Its docs builder writes the URL for us, so we never guess parameter names.
In Hoppscotch, set the method to GET and paste the forecast address. Hoppscotch splits it into the same parameter table you'll fill on an HTTP step later.
The time zone matters. Without it, tomorrow could mean tomorrow in London, and late at night you'd read the wrong day.
Press Send. We want status two hundred, OK, and a JSON body.
Read the shape. The daily lists line up by position: position zero is today, position one is tomorrow.
Now a simple rule: fifty per cent or more, the riders pack covers. Seventy is above fifty, so tonight's message is pack covers. No AI needed; it's a number against a threshold.
Break it on purpose. Remove latitude and you get a four hundred, Bad Request. Misspell forecast and you get a four oh four, wrong address.
Now flip roles. Webhook.site gives you a unique URL that plays Harvest Lane's system, and records anything sent to it.
Send a pretend payment notice for order HL-0042 and watch it appear instantly. That's a webhook: the doorbell, not the mailbox.
steps.data: request received with headers and body

steps.say: One trap: the amount is in kobo, not naira. One million two hundred and fifty thousand kobo is twelve thousand five hundred naira, so check the unit before any maths.

walk.end: You've been the client and the server. Every HTTP step and webhook trigger in this course is just this, wrapped in a nicer screen.
